finding.claim: Realm SSRF guard (validateRealm) is bypassed by HTTP redirects from the token endpoint; the client follows a 302 from an attacker-controlled https realm to internal http hosts such as 169.254.169.254 and reflects JSON token fields as a Bearer token to the attacker's registry.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled registry 401 WWW-Authenticate Bearer realm header (client.go:309-361)
finding.sink: fetchDistributionToken GET to realm (client.go:418-434), redirects followed via c.send (client.go:136-159); token decode (client.go:446-459) and reuse as Authorization: Bearer (client.go:368-377)

trace.note: challenge read from attacker-controlled Www-Authenticate header
validateRealm applied only to the initial realm string
validator checks scheme and IP-literal of the realm URL only; DNS names not blocked
fetchBearerToken invoked with unvalidated redirect path
GET to realm with no redirect policy
CheckRedirect only strips Authorization on cross-origin hops; does not re-run validateRealm
JSON decoded into token/access_token fields (case-insensitive key match)
returned token set as Authorization: Bearer on retry to the attacker registry

finding.guards_checked: validateRealm scheme check (client.go:229-233) and IP-literal check (client.go:235-242) apply only to the initial realm, not redirect targets; no CheckRedirect in the codebase returns ErrUseLastResponse (grep); errutil.ParseErrorResponse (errutil.go:34-47) limits body reflection to JSON errors; TLS verification limits some internal targets; impact limited to blind SSRF plus partial token exposure; requires IMDSv1 and a guessable role name for the AWS case.

finding.claim: Descriptor digests from untrusted manifests are interpolated into request URL paths without validation in Fetch, Delete, referrers, and Tag paths, enabling path/query injection with the victim's credentials against the same registry host.
finding.source: Layer/config/index descriptor digest from attacker-published manifest JSON (repository.go:1423, utils.go:120 decodeJSON) passed by the caller to Fetch/Delete/Tag
finding.sink: blobStore.Fetch URL build (repository.go:752-754); manifestStore.Fetch (repository.go:1114-1116); delete (repository.go:716-722); referrersByAPI (repository.go:527-530); Tag->Fetch (repository.go:1318)

trace.note: Repository.Fetch passes target descriptor straight to blobStore
buildRepositoryBlobURL concatenates digest into URL path
path built with strings.Join, no escaping or validation
same unvalidated pattern in delete() using DELETE method

finding.guards_checked: No digest validation on these paths. Contrast: blobStore.Resolve (repository.go:1001) calls ref.Digest(); ParseReference (repository.go:369-402) validates; buildReferrersTag (referrers.go:108) validates desc.Digest only in the fallback path. Server-side token scope still applies, and routing of traversed paths on a real registry is unverified.
